findings.problem: SkipLink is rendered unconditionally as the first child of UnsavedChangesProvider, but its href="#main-content" target only exists once a routed page renders PageLayout's <main> under <Outlet>, which itself requires `user` to be truthy. While `!user || !isConfigFetched` (the initial load / unauthenticated window), the app renders only the Spinner — #main-content does not exist in the DOM.
findings.impact: A keyboard or screen-reader user who tabs to and activates the skip link during app load or before authentication gets no effect: focus stays put and nothing happens, defeating the WCAG 2.4.1 mechanism this ticket exists to add, for the entire duration of that window.
findings.recommendation: Guard SkipLink so it only renders (or its href/behavior is meaningful) once the main landmark can exist — e.g. render it only when `user && isConfigFetched`, or add an onClick handler that no-ops gracefully when the target is absent.

findings.problem: SkipLink relies solely on native anchor fragment navigation plus tabIndex={-1} on the target to shift focus; there is no onClick handler calling .focus() explicitly. Some browsers (notably a documented history in Safari) do not move focus to non-form elements via hash navigation even with tabindex=-1. No automated test exercises the actual focus-shift because jsdom does not implement native hash-navigation focus behavior — the existing tests only assert static attributes/classes.
findings.impact: If the assumption doesn't hold in a currently-supported browser, the skip link's core mechanism (moving focus past repeated blocks) silently fails for those users, and no test would catch it.
findings.recommendation: Decide whether to add an explicit onClick handler (`preventDefault` + `document.getElementById('main-content')?.focus()`) for cross-browser robustness, which would also make the focus-shift directly unit-testable in jsdom.

findings.problem: The visibility classes use `focus:not-sr-only` rather than `focus-visible:not-sr-only`, so the link becomes visible on any focus event (including a stray `.focus()` call or non-keyboard focus), not only keyboard-driven focus.
findings.impact: The skip link can visibly flash into view for interactions where a keyboard-only affordance isn't expected, which is a minor but real deviation from current skip-link UX best practice.
findings.recommendation: Decide whether to switch to `focus-visible:` classes to restrict visibility to keyboard-driven focus, matching modern skip-link conventions.
